issues.body: The new branch only validates a dict-shaped gold_count when `q` itself is a dict. Tasks cc03 and cc05 instead have a single string query with dict-shaped `gold_keys`; cc03 has an integer aggregate gold_count and cc05 has `gold_count: 3`. They therefore miss both the existing list-gold branch and the new multi-part branch. Any non-empty one-row result passes even if cc03 returns incorrect event/artifact values or cc05 returns incorrect claim/document/method counts. This leaves the validator unable to prove material refreshed gold answers and permits future fixture drift to remain silent.
issues.fix_hint: Parse and compare the returned multi-column/grouped values against the dict-shaped expected values for every dict-gold task, including cc03 and cc05. Add a focused regression test that mutates one expected category value (or supplies a deliberately wrong query result) and demonstrates validation fails; also test the correct result passes.
issues.title: Dict-shaped gold answers remain effectively unchecked for cc03 and cc05

verdict.summary: The fixture refresh is directionally sound, and the new th03 per-part check closes the specific validation gap described. However, validation remains non-exhaustive for other dict-shaped gold answers: cc03 and cc05 still pass when their actual category values are wrong because their SELECT is a string, their gold_keys is a dict, and neither newly added branch applies. Since the PR presents validate_tasks.py as proving the refreshed gold corpus, this is a major test-validity gap.
